task:
Produce a decision-ready delivery forecast in roughly 180-280 words. Use only the supplied model and facts; this is an output-only exercise with no repository investigation or execution.

Today is working-time origin 0. Two required adapter tasks, A and B, are ready to start. Each requires a specialist for its entire duration; each duration is independently 2 working days with probability 0.8 or 6 working days with probability 0.2. These are elicited model inputs, not calibrated historical frequencies. Task durations include each adapter's coding, tests and review, but exclude the following shared work.

After both tasks finish, an independent team performs exactly 1 working day of combined acceptance. The resulting artifact can deploy and receive final acceptance only at working-time points 4, 8, 12 or 16. A result ready exactly at a slot may use that slot; missing it requires waiting for the next. There are no holidays, other queues, rework, or omitted activities in this illustrative model. Completion means deployment acceptance, not merge.

Only one qualified specialist is reserved full time from origin 0. A and B each require that person's full capacity and cannot overlap; either order is permitted. Their duration draws remain independent.

The sponsor's target is deployment acceptance by time 8, and asks you to promise it because each task has P80 of 2 days. No commitment has been made. Give the model probability of meeting the target and the project's P80, defined as the earliest completion time with cumulative probability at least 0.8. Explain the schedule that yields them, distinguish a model forecast from a promise, and name a material update trigger.
